standard.title: Origin, Content, Purpose and Context of Sources
standard.description: identify the origin and content of sources, and explain the purpose and context of primary and secondary sources
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify the origin and content of sources and explain the purpose and context of primary and secondary sources in a Year 9 inquiry context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the origin and content of a range of source types, explain their purpose and historical context, and describe stylistic elements of sources to inform meaning.

nodes.label: Origin, content and context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the historical context of a source, identify its origin and content, and identify any gaps or inaccuracies.
nodes.minimum_width: For at least one source, explain its historical context, identify its origin and content, and identify at least one gap or potential inaccuracy.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the historical context of sources and identify gaps or inaccuracies — asking what the source cannot tell us as well as what it can; identify the origin (who created it, when, where) and content (what it contains, what it describes) of primary and secondary sources across a range of types used in Year 10 History.
wider: Apply origin and context analysis to a source whose historical context has been contested or misrepresented — examining how knowing the correct context changes the source's meaning

Analyse sources produced by or about First Nations Australians — examining how understanding the cultural context of production (a petition, an oral account, a sacred object) requires different analytical approaches than standard documentary analysis
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding context is the prerequisite for purpose analysis in Node 2. Students who analyse purpose without first establishing context typically produce circular or superficial purpose statements — 'the author wrote this to inform readers' — rather than historically grounded purpose analysis.

response_modes.reason: Use the OPVL (Origin, Purpose, Value, Limitation) or similar structured framework as a scaffold for context-before-purpose analysis. Explicitly require students to establish context before attempting purpose — model what changes in the purpose analysis when context is established.

success_criteria: Identify the origin of at least one source (who created it, when, in what context)
Explain the historical context in which the source was produced
Identify at least one gap or potential inaccuracy in the source and explain what might have produced it

nodes.label: Purpose and stylistic elements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse the intent of the author and the features of a source to determine its purpose, and describe stylistic elements to inform the meaning of sources.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse the intent of the author of at least one source and explain its purpose; describe at least one stylistic element of a source and explain what it contributes to meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse the intent of the author and the features of a source to determine purpose — asking why it was made, for what audience, and to what effect; describe stylistic elements of sources such as artistic technique, architectural features, or textual structure to inform the meaning of sources; apply this analysis across both primary and secondary source types.
wider: Apply purpose analysis to a source whose purpose has been contested or misread — such as a propaganda image or a manipulated photograph — examining how knowledge of intent changes interpretation

Analyse a non-documentary source type (photograph, artwork, material artefact, oral testimony) and compare the purpose/stylistic analysis process with that used for written documents — examining what each source type reveals and conceals

response_modes.reason: Apply purpose and stylistic analysis across multiple source types within one inquiry — written document, photograph, material artefact, oral testimony — to build a repertoire of analytical approaches. Each source type reveals different dimensions of purpose.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Applying purpose and stylistic analysis across diverse source types builds genuinely transferable historical source analysis skills — a capability that operates across every K-strand topic in the course and into senior history.
success_criteria: Analyse the intent of the author of at least one source and explain its purpose in relation to its historical context
Describe at least one stylistic element of a source (artistic, architectural, or textual) and explain what it contributes to meaning
Apply purpose analysis across at least two different source types and compare what each type reveals
